Aethera Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Aethera Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold, as background noise may be transmitted. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aethera Therapeutics' financial results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Maria Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Johnathan Hale, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Scientific Officer and Head of R&D.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Maria Ramirez, CEO of Aethera Therapeutics.

Dr. Maria Ramirez, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Aethera Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the Q3, driven by robust demand across our oncology franchise, particularly our next-generation antibody-drug conjugates, successful pipeline milestones, and disciplined execution amid a dynamic biotech landscape. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, positioning us to capture meaningful share in high-growth areas like precision oncology and genetic medicines.

Today, I'll provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives. We're particularly excited about our lead ADC programs like AETH-301 and VG-101 analogs, and their potential to drive multi-billion peak sales in solid tumors.

I'll now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Johnathan Hale, CFO:
Thank you, Maria. As Maria mentioned, we had a solid Q3. Revenue for the quarter was $2.85 billion, an increase of 28% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by strong oncology sales growth, label expansions, and milestone payments from key partnerships.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $1.45 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $580 million, or $1.85 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.6 billion, reflecting continued investment in R&D to support our pipeline while achieving operational efficiencies. We continue to invest heavily in innovation to fuel our diversified portfolio. Our cash position remains strong at $4.2 billion.

Thank you, Maria, and good morning, everyone. I'm thrilled to walk you through what was an exceptional quarter, underscoring the strength of our diversified portfolio and the accelerating momentum in our oncology and gene therapy franchises. We delivered results that significantly exceeded our guidance and consensus expectations, driven by robust demand for our blockbuster assets, successful commercial launches, and disciplined cost management amid a favorable macro environment for innovative therapies.

Let me start with the top-line highlights. Total worldwide revenue came in at $2.85 billion, up a stellar 28% year-over-year and 8% on a constant-currency basis, smashing our prior guidance midpoint of $2.6 billion and Wall Street's consensus of $2.72 billion. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, reflecting the resilience of our high-margin products in a market still grappling with post-pandemic supply chain normalization and biosimilar erosion pressures seen across peers like Pfizer with Ibrance or Bristol Myers Squibb navigating Opdivo headwinds.

Breaking it down by therapeutic area—our North Star segmentation—oncology revenue soared to $1.92 billion, representing 67% of total sales and growing 35% YoY. The standout here is our PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor, AETH-101 (neratinib axitinib), which posted $1.45 billion in net sales, up 42% YoY and capturing an estimated 18% U.S. market share in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and melanoma combos, per IQVIA data. Volume growth accounted for 65% of this uplift, fueled by expanded label indications from our pivotal Phase III AETHER-LUNG trial readout last quarter, while pricing held steady at around 4% net realization after rebates. Complementing this, our next-gen ADC, AETH-205 (belzutifan conjugate), ramped to $320 million in its first full quarter post-FDA approval, hitting our accelerated launch trajectory with peak sales potential north of $3 billion annually, positioning us to challenge Roche's Kadcyla in HER2-positive breast cancer.

In rare diseases and immunology, we generated $680 million, up 15% YoY, led by AETH-078 (venglustat) for Fabry disease, which exceeded $450 million despite a temporary supply hiccup in EMEA that we've now resolved via our expanded Singapore manufacturing hub. Gene therapy remains a high-conviction growth engine: AETH-GT3, our AAV-based candidate for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), contributed $150 million from early U.S. access programs, with enrollment complete in our global Phase III GT-SMA pivotal trial—data expected H1 2025, which could mirror the transformative uptake of Novartis' Zolgensma.

Gross margins expanded to a record 87.2%, up 320 basis points YoY, benefiting from higher-mix oncology sales, manufacturing efficiencies at our Devens, MA facility, and lower COGS from in-sourcing plasmid production. Operating expenses grew 12% YoY to $1.1 billion, in line with our R&D intensity target of 28-30% of revenue—we invested heavily in next-gen modalities, including $250 million in AI-accelerated small-molecule discovery via our partnership with Insilico Medicine, yielding three IND-ready candidates in our Q2 pipeline update.

This flow-through delivered adjusted non-GAAP EPS of $1.85, crushing expectations of $1.62 and up 32% YoY. On a GAAP basis, EPS was $1.45, reflecting one-time M&A costs from our $4.2 billion acquisition of SynthoGen, bolstering our CRISPR-Cas13 platform for RNA editing. Free cash flow was robust at $1.1 billion, supporting $750 million in share repurchases under our ongoing $5 billion authorization, with net debt to EBITDA now at a pristine 1.2x.

Turning to regional dynamics, the U.S. drove 72% of revenue at $2.05 billion, up 31% YoY, propelled by payer access wins—including full Medicare Part D coverage for AETH-101 combos—and a favorable IRA negotiation outlook for our '25-'27 pricing cycle. Medicare net pricing for AETH-101 stabilized at 82% of WAC, better than the industry average erosion of 15-20% seen with Eli Lilly's Mounjaro. In EMEA, sales hit $520 million, +22% CER, with strong reimbursement in Germany and France for AETH-078, though we saw modest headwinds from Italy's AIFA review delays. Asia-Pacific grew 18% CER to $280 million, led by Japan launch of AETH-101 via our Eisai alliance, which triggered a $150 million milestone, and China volumes up 25% despite ongoing CFDA inspections—our Shanghai J-V with CSPC is now at full capacity for biosimilar-free AETH-205 production.

Strategically, we're leaning into three pillars shaping our industry: precision oncology, platform innovation, and global access. On precision, our AETHER-OMICS companion diagnostic platform, integrated with NGS from Illumina partners, drove 45% of AETH-101 scripts last quarter, enhancing response rates to 68% ORR in KRAS-mutated NSCLC per real-world evidence. Technologically, we're deploying federated ML models across 50+ TB of multi-omics data from our SynthoGen integration, slashing hit-to-lead timelines by 40%—early proof in our SHP2 inhibitor program, advancing to Phase I for RAS-driven cancers.

Regionally, we're addressing China’s volume-based procurement (VBP) risks head-on with localized trials; our APAC pipeline now has 12 assets in late-stage development, targeting 20% of FY25 revenue from emerging markets. Sustainability-wise, we reduced Scope 1/2 emissions 25% YoY via green chemistry at our Ireland site, aligning with EU CSRD mandates and appealing to ESG investors.

Key takeaways? One: Our oncology engine is firing on all cylinders, with AETH-101 on track for $6 billion in FY24 sales and multi-blockbuster potential from ADCs and bispecifics. Two: Pipeline derisking is accelerating—70% Phase III success probability per our models, bolstered by AI, positions us for 3-5 approvals in 2025, including GT3 for SMA. Three: Balance sheet fortress enables bolt-on M&A, like the SynthoGen deal, without diluting ROIC, which hit 22%.

Now, turning to our R&D expenses and pipeline investment priorities for the quarter. I'll hand it over to our Chief Scientific Officer and Head of R&D, Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide the details on how we're fueling our innovation engine amid a dynamic biotech landscape.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thanks, Johnathan. In Q3, we reported R&D expenses of $452 million, representing a 28% year-over-year increase from $353 million in the prior-year period. This acceleration reflects our deliberate ramp-up in late-stage clinical investments and early-stage platform technologies, consistent with our strategy to build a diversified, high-value pipeline targeting areas of massive unmet need. As a percentage of our Q3 revenue of $2.85 billion, R&D came in at 32%, up from 28% last year, underscoring our biotech pure-play focus where innovation drives long-term value creation—much like we've seen with peers such as Regeneron and Vertex in their oncology and rare disease breakthroughs.

For the full year 2024, we're maintaining our guidance for R&D spend in the range of $1.85 billion to $1.95 billion, or approximately 30% of our projected revenue midpoint of $11.0 billion. This includes about $1.1 billion in externalized costs for clinical trials and manufacturing scale-up, with the balance in internal discovery and preclinical efforts. Quarter-over-quarter, we saw a 12% sequential increase from Q2's $403 million, driven primarily by patient dosing in our Phase 3 oncology programs and CMC work for upcoming BLA filings.

Let me break this down by our key investment priorities, which align with three strategic pillars: therapeutic focus, modalities and technologies, and operational efficiencies.

First, therapeutic priorities. Oncology remains our North Star, accounting for 45% of our R&D spend, or roughly $203 million in Q3. We're laser-focused on solid tumors, where we've seen explosive growth akin to Merck's Keytruda franchise or AstraZeneca's Tagrisso dominance. Key here is BNT-456, our next-generation antibody-drug conjugate—or ADC—in Phase 3 for non-small cell lung cancer and HER2-positive breast cancer. Topline data expected Q4 2024 could position it as a best-in-class follower to Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu, with projected peak sales exceeding $2.5 billion. We're also advancing two bispecific T-cell engagers in Phase 2 for hematologic malignancies, targeting the CAR-T refractory space.

Immunology and rare diseases capture 25% of spend, or $113 million, with heavy emphasis on genetic medicines. Our lead asset, BN-RD101—a AAV9 gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy—mirrors Novartis' Zolgensma success but with a redesigned capsid for reduced immunogenicity and broader CNS penetration. We're enrolling rapidly in a global Phase 3 pivotal, with interim futility analysis passing last month. In immunology, we're investing in IL-23/IL-17 dual inhibitors for psoriasis and IBD, aiming to challenge AbbVie's Skyrizi in a market projected to hit $15 billion by 2028 per Evaluate Pharma.

Infectious diseases, at 15% or $68 million, leverages our mRNA platform post our COVID-19 collaboration tailwinds. BN-VAX-23, a universal flu-coronavirus combo vaccine, entered Phase 2b this quarter, with data readouts in H1 2025. We've allocated 10% here to pandemic preparedness, partnering with BARDA for next-gen Lassa and Nipah candidates.

The remaining 15% spans neurology (e.g., anti-amyloid bispecifics chasing Eli Lilly's donanemab momentum) and cardiovascular (PCSK9 RNAi follow-ons).

Second, on modalities and technical initiatives. We're shifting ~40% of our pipeline value to next-gen modalities—up from 25% two years ago—prioritizing scalability and durability over traditional small molecules, which now represent just 30% of spend. Cell and gene therapies are 25%, ADCs and bispecifics 10%, and mRNA/RNAi platforms 5%. A big enabler is our AI/ML drug discovery engine, powered by a Schrödinger-tenant on AWS, which has cut hit-to-lead timelines by 40% and identified three novel kinase inhibitors now in IND-enabling studies. We're also deploying high-throughput CRISPR screening for synthetic lethality targets in oncology, similar to Revolution Medicines' RAS programs.

Regionally, we're optimizing for speed and diversity. 55% of trials are U.S.-based for FDA alignment, 25% in Europe via our EMA PRIME designations, and 20% in Asia-Pacific—primarily China and South Korea—for faster enrollment in oncology and rare diseases. This mirrors Gilead's approach in HIV and has shaved 6-9 months off timelines, with our Shanghai site fully operational for CMC and early Phase 1.

Strategically, these investments are about derisking for sustained growth. We're prioritizing assets with >$1 billion peak sales potential and probability of success above 25%—per our internal models benchmarked against McKinsey's biopharma database. To manage burn, we've realized 15% cost efficiencies through virtualized trials (à la Teladoc integrations) and milestone-based partnerships, including our $500 million upfront deal with CRISPR Therapeutics for in vivo editing and a $300 million alliance with Beam Therapeutics for base editing in liver diseases. M&A remains opportunistic; we closed the $1.2 billion acquisition of RareGenix last month, adding three Phase 2 assets and bolstering our gene therapy vector supply chain amid CMO shortages.

Looking ahead, we expect R&D intensity to moderate to 28% of revenue by 2026 as royalties from our partnered assets—like the BTK degrader out-licensed to Sanofi—ramp up. But we'll continue outspending peers on innovation, with 12 Phase 2/3 readouts and four potential filings in the next 18 months. This positions Aethera to deliver 15-20% CAGR in pipeline value through the decade.

Now, as we wrap up a transformative Q3, I'm pleased to provide our updated full-year 2024 revenue guidance and outline the key catalysts that position us for accelerated growth into 2025 and beyond. Our results continue to validate the strength of our oncology franchise, particularly VG-101, our next-generation antibody-drug conjugate—or ADC—targeting HER2-positive solid tumors, which is tracking ahead of our internal models and mirroring the blockbuster trajectory we've seen with peers like AstraZeneca's Enhertu.

First, a quick recap on Q3 performance to set the context. We delivered net product revenues of $682 million for the segment, up 28% year-over-year and 5% above the midpoint of our prior guidance. This was driven by VG-101 global net sales of $450 million—a 45% sequential quarterly ramp—fueled by strong U.S. demand following our label expansion into gastric cancer last quarter, and initial EU uptake post-EMA approval in June. Royalty and milestone revenues added $52 million, including a $40 million milestone from our partner Roche on VG-101 ex-U.S. commercialization progress. Collaboration revenues came in at $180 million, bolstered by upfront payments from our recent ADC payload licensing deal with Pfizer.

Geographically, the U.S. represented 72% of net product sales at $490 million, reflecting robust reimbursement dynamics under Medicare Part B and our J-code assignment earlier this year, which minimized patient access hurdles. Europe contributed 18% or $123 million, with sequential growth in Germany and France offsetting softer UK volumes amid NHS pricing pressures. Rest-of-World, at 10% or $69 million, saw double-digit growth in Japan via our Eisai partnership, though China remains nascent at just 2% of total, pending NMPA approval expected Q1 2025.

Turning to full-year 2024 guidance. We're raising the midpoint across the board. We now expect consolidated revenues of $11.8 billion to $12.0 billion, representing 24% to 30% growth over 2023's $9.5 billion. This compares favorably to our prior range of $11.4 billion to $11.8 billion and reflects VG-101 outperformance, partially offset by anticipated biosimilar erosion on our legacy immunology asset, VG-201, where U.S. volumes are down 15% quarter-over-quarter due to Amgen's Steflara biosimilar launch.

Breaking it down:
- Net product sales: $9.4 billion to $9.6 billion (80% of total), with VG-101 driving 65% or roughly $6.1 billion to $6.2 billion. We're guiding to U.S. sales of $6.7 billion to $6.9 billion (up 40% YoY), EU at $2.3 billion to $2.5 billion (up 55% YoY), and RoW at $1.0 billion to $1.1 billion.
- Royalty and milestone revenues: $1.9 billion to $2.1 billion, including $100 million in VG-101 milestones from Roche and Eisai.
- Collaboration revenues: $2.5 billion to $2.7 billion, anchored by our Pfizer ADC deal and ongoing CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing partnerships.

For Q4 specifically, we guide to $2.95 billion to $3.05 billion in total revenues, implying seasonality in VG-101 loading doses but strength in maintenance therapy uptake. Gross margins remain healthy at 86% to 88%, supported by manufacturing scale-up at our Singapore facility, where we've increased ADC linker production capacity by 50% YTD through continuous flow chemistry tech.

Now, to the key upcoming catalysts that de-risk our trajectory and unlock multi-billar peak sales potential. We're laser-focused on three pillars: pipeline advancement, geographic expansion, and strategic partnerships, all amid a favorable macro tailwind from the GLP-1 obesity wave indirectly boosting oncology trial enrollment via improved patient comorbidities management.

1. Regulatory Milestones (Highest Probability/Impact): 
   - Q1 2025 PDUFA for VG-102, our bispecific ADC for EGFR-mutant NSCLC. Topline Phase 3 data from the VISTA-3 trial showed a 52% ORR and 14-month PFS versus 9 months for Tagrisso monotherapy—statistically significant with p<0.001. Approval here could add $800 million in peak U.S. sales by 2028, per our models, and we've already filed in EU and Japan.
   - Q2 2025 topline readout from the HEMO-GENE Phase 3 trial for VG-301, our AAV-based gene therapy for hemophilia A. Interim futility analysis passed in Q3, and we're projecting 80% durable Factor VIII expression at 52 weeks, positioning us against BioMarin's Roctavian in a $5 billion TAM. Success here triggers a $200 million milestone from our co-developer, Sanofi.

2. Commercial and Label Expansion Catalysts:
   - VG-101 sBLA for frontline breast cancer: FDA acceptance with priority review; decision by March 2025. This could double addressable patients, driving U.S. peak sales to $3.5 billion, akin to Enhertu's trajectory.
   - China NMPA approval and launch for VG-101: Q1 2025 filing acceptance, with first sales Q3. China oncology ADC market is exploding—up 150% YoY per IQVIA—and our Eisai JV gives us a head start over imports.
   - Biosimilar defense: Filing our VG-201 patent thicket extensions under the Inflation Reduction Act's patent dance provisions, aiming to delay full erosion until 2029.

3. Strategic and Technical Initiatives:
   - Pfizer ADC alliance expansion: $500 million upfront received in Q3; option exercise on two next-gen payloads by YE2024, with potential $2 billion in milestones/royalties. This de-risks R&D spend, which we're guiding to $950 million for FY2024 (36% of revs).
   - AI-Driven Discovery Platform: Our HelixAI engine, leveraging AlphaFold3-inspired protein modeling, has nominated three IND-ready candidates in immuno-oncology. First FIH data Q4 2025.
   - Manufacturing Resilience: Onshoring 30% of U.S. fill-finish via our North Carolina site, mitigating supply chain risks seen in peers like Eli Lilly's Mounjaro shortages.

In summary, our raised guidance reflects execution today, while these catalysts—PDUFA, Phase 3 readouts, and partnerships—set up 35%+ CAGR through 2027, targeting $18 billion in revenue with 25%+ operating margins. We're well-positioned in high-growth areas like ADCs and gene therapies, even as IRA price controls loom on small molecules post-2026.

For FY24 guidance, margins steady at 86-88%, R&D ~29%. Risks remain around biosimilar entrants for legacy assets and macro inflation, but our 65% gross margin buffer and hedging provide insulation.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Maria.

Dr. Maria Ramirez, CEO:
Thank you, Johnathan and Elena. I'll now turn to our strategic priorities for the balance of 2024 and into 2025, as well as our outlook. As you know, Aethera Therapeutics remains laser-focused on our mission to deliver transformative therapies in oncology and rare genetic diseases, leveraging our proprietary platform in next-generation antibody-drug conjugates—ADCs—and bispecific T-cell engagers. In a market where global oncology spending is projected to exceed $375 billion by 2027 according to IQVIA, we're positioning ourselves to capture meaningful share through disciplined execution across R&D, commercial operations, and strategic partnerships.

Let me outline our top three strategic priorities.

First, advancing our late-stage pipeline to key catalysts. We're prioritizing our lead ADC candidate, AETH-301, a next-gen HER2-targeted conjugate with a novel cleavable linker that demonstrated a 68% objective response rate in our pivotal Phase 3 HERTHA trial in metastatic breast cancer, surpassing benchmarks set by Enhertu from Daiichi Sankyo and AstraZeneca. We remain on track for a BLA submission to the FDA in Q1 2025, with a PDUFA target in Q4 2025. Peak sales potential here exceeds $2.5 billion annually in a TAM of over $15 billion for HER2-positive solid tumors. Complementing this, our bispecific AETH-450 in non-small cell lung cancer—aimed at PD-1 x VEGF—hit 52% ORR in the ongoing Phase 2/3 APEX study, and we'll initiate a registrational trial in Q2 2025 partnering with the FDA under their Breakthrough Therapy Designation.

In rare diseases, AETH-720, our gene-editing therapy using base editing technology licensed from Beam Therapeutics, showed 87% durability in liver enzyme normalization at 12 months in our Phase 2 trial for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. We're accelerating enrollment for Phase 3 readout in mid-2026, tapping into a $10 billion addressable market underserved by current standards like GSK's Kamada.

We've allocated $1.2 billion—or 28% of our projected 2024 revenue—to R&D, up 15% YoY, with a pipeline of 12 clinical assets, seven of which are in Phase 2 or beyond. Our success rate from Phase 1 to approval stands at 25%, well above the industry average of 10-15% per BIO data.

Second, driving commercial excellence and market expansion. Our flagship product, AETH-200—the first approved ADC for triple-negative breast cancer—continues to outperform, delivering $850 million in 2024 YTD sales, a 42% YoY increase, fueled by label expansion into adjuvant settings and uptake in community oncology practices. U.S. net price per patient rose 8% to $145,000 sequentially, despite payer pushback, thanks to our value-based contracting with CVS Caremark and Express Scripts covering 65% of lives.

Regionally, North America accounts for 72% of sales, with TRx share climbing to 28% in 2L/3L TNBC per IQVIA NPA data, closing the gap on Trodelvy's 35% dominance. In Europe, we're navigating EMA reimbursement hurdles—reimbursement in Germany and France now covers 55% of eligible patients post-2024 IQWiG assessment—but expect full ramp-up with positive NICE guidance in the UK by year-end. China remains a growth engine: our partnership with Innovent Biologics has driven $120 million in milestone and royalty revenue YTD, with AETH-200 launching commercially there in Q4 via the NMPA fast-track. Emerging markets like Brazil and India contribute 5% of sales today but are targeted to hit 12% by 2026 through generics partnerships and compassionate use programs.

We're also investing $300 million in U.S. manufacturing scale-up at our new Devens, MA facility, which uses continuous perfusion bioreactors to boost ADC yields by 40%, mitigating supply constraints that plagued peers like Seagen pre-Pfizer acquisition.

Third, forging strategic alliances and operational efficiency. M&A remains opportunistic—we closed the $1.8 billion acquisition of SynthoBio last quarter, adding three preclinical ADCs and their exosome delivery platform, accretive to EPS by 2026. On partnerships, our expanded collaboration with Regeneron on multi-specific antibodies generated $200 million upfront, with opt-ins valued at $3 billion in milestones. To counter biosimilar erosion—expected to shave 20-25% off our legacy immunology portfolio like AETH-100 by 2027—we're rightsizing our U.S. sales force by 12% while redirecting 60% to high-growth launches, targeting SG&A at 22% of revenue.

Sustainability is embedded: our ESG score rose to AA from MSCI, driven by 95% renewable energy in manufacturing and a 30% reduction in Scope 1 emissions, aligning with EU CSRD mandates.

Now, turning to outlook. For Q4 2024, we expect total revenue of $2.95 billion to $3.05 billion, representing 22% YoY growth at the midpoint, driven by AETH-200 uptake and $150 million in new milestone payments. Full-year 2024 revenue guidance is narrowed to $11.8 billion to $12.0 billion, up 24% from 2023, with adjusted non-GAAP EPS of $7.40 to $7.60.

Looking to 2025, we're guiding to revenue of $14.7 billion to $15.6 billion, a 25% increase at midpoint, assuming AETH-301 approval and launch in H2, plus 30% AETH-200 growth. Adjusted EPS of $9.40 to $9.75 reflects R&D reinvestment but margin expansion to 42% gross via manufacturing efficiencies. Risks include clinical setbacks—though our LOA risk-adjusted NPV is $18 billion—and U.S. pricing reforms under the Inflation Reduction Act, which we model as a 5-7% headwind on Medicare Part D volumes post-2026.

In summary, with a $30 billion market cap, fortress balance sheet of $4.2 billion cash, and debt-to-EBITDA at 1.8x, we're executing with precision in this dynamic industry. We're not just riding trends like the $100 billion ADC wave or obesity spillover into cardio-renal—we're shaping them. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee, Morgan Stanley:
Thanks, and good morning. Great quarter—congrats. On the R&D side, with the 28% YoY increase and heavy oncology weighting, how are you thinking about prioritizing between ADCs like BNT-456 and gene therapies like BN-RD101 if we see any budget pressures next year?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Scientific Officer:
Good morning, David. Thanks for the question. Our prioritization remains anchored to assets with over $1 billion peak sales and >25% PoS, as I outlined. Oncology gets 45% because of the TAM and our differentiated payloads, but gene therapies like BN-RD101 are high-conviction with Zolgensma-like durability. No trade-offs planned; efficiencies from AI and partnerships like CRISPR keep us on track for the $1.85-1.95B guidance without cuts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen, Goldman Sachs:
Hi, team. On catalysts, the VG-102 PDUFA in Q1 '25 sounds promising—can you elaborate on the label potential versus Enhertu and any combo data upcoming?

Johnathan Hale, CFO:
Hi Lisa, thanks. VG-102's 52% ORR and 14-month PFS in EGFR-mutant NSCLC positions it as a combo enabler over Tagrisso alone. Label would cover frontline maintenance post-chemo, adding $800M peak U.S. by '28. We're planning combos with our bispecifics; early data H2 '25. This de-risks our 35% CAGR outlook.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel, JPMorgan:
Morning, all. With raised guidance to $11.8-12B and biosimilar headwinds on VG-201, how much buffer do you have for IRA impacts, and thoughts on M&A post-SynthoGen?

Dr. Maria Ramirez, CEO:
Mike, great question. Our $18B risk-adjusted NPV gives ample buffer—IRA modeled at 5-7% post-'26, offset by ADC ramps and partnerships like Pfizer's $2B milestones. M&A opportunistic, like SynthoGen or RareGenix, targeting vectors and payloads to fortify supply amid shortages. Balance sheet supports more without dilution.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Dr. Maria Ramirez, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Aethera Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
